# omadafusion_ssid_schedule (Resource)

Attaches a WLAN schedule to an existing SSID, e.g. to switch guest Wi-Fi off after hours. Only the schedule fields change; the SSID and its other settings are read and sent back unchanged. Destroying this resource disables the schedule, leaving the SSID broadcasting normally.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "omadafusion_ssid" "guest" {
  name = "Guest WiFi"
}

# Guest Wi-Fi only broadcasts during business hours.
resource "omadafusion_ssid_schedule" "guest" {
  ssid_id       = data.omadafusion_ssid.guest.id
  time_range_id = omadafusion_time_range.business_hours.id
  action        = "radio_on"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `ssid_id` (String) SSID ID, e.g. from `data.omadafusion_ssid`.
- `time_range_id` (String) ID of an `omadafusion_time_range`.

### Optional

- `action` (String) `radio_on` (default): broadcast only inside the time range. `radio_off`: stop broadcasting inside the time range.
- `site` (String) Site name or ID. Defaults to the provider `site`. Changing it forces a new resource.
- `wlan_id` (String) WLAN group ID. Looked up from the SSID when omitted.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Same as `ssid_id`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# <ssid_id> or <site>/<ssid_id>
terraform import omadafusion_ssid_schedule.guest Default/64f0c0ffee00000000000001
```
